key_insight: Wasserstein approximation by measures supported on orthogonal axes identifies a basis for sparse data representation, with near-parametric frame recovery under mild assumptions.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a principled way to select sparse-representation axes within a subspace, complementing PCA for unsupervised learning.
method: Approximate the data distribution using measures supported on the axes of an orthogonal frame.
Optimize a nonsmooth objective over the orthogonal group using empirical risk minimization or locally initialized stochastic gradients.
Use a coarsely Lipschitz gradient bound to handle the mismatch between smooth population and nonsmooth empirical objectives.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovery guarantees of Õ_d(n⁻¹ᐟ²) for both approaches and supporting numerical experiments, without specifying datasets or quantitative results.
watch_item: The stochastic-gradient guarantee requires local initialization, and the stated rate hides dimension-dependent factors.
paper_title: Wasserstein approximation of measures via orthogonal frames: statistical and computational complexities
